topics.description: The historical Portuguese kingdom that sponsored maritime exploration and formed the basis of Portugal's overseas empire.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Many religions have been practiced in India during its long history. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] The emperor Akbar the Great repealed the jizya, a tax on all subjects of the Mughal Empire that did not adhere to this religion, which the Mughal Empire spread by building mosques.
parts.answer: Islam [accept Muslims; accept Sunni Islam or Shi'a Islam]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This Maurya Emperor converted to Buddhism after witnessing mass deaths in his bloody conquest of Kalinga, according to his "rock edicts."
parts.answer: Ashoka the Great [or Ashoka Maurya; accept Asoka in place of "Ashoka"]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Vasco da Gama, an explorer from this country, spread Christianity in India after sailing to it by rounding the tip of Africa. Another explorer from this country almost completed his circumnavigation of the world, but was killed by Filipino natives.

topics.description: Mao Zedong's mass political campaign in China from 1966 to 1976 that targeted perceived bourgeois, revisionist, and counterrevolutionary elements and caused widespread upheaval.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This leader denounced the Five Black Categories, which included “rich peasants” and “rightists.” This leader began political campaigns with photoshoots of himself crossing a river. This leader temporarily encouraged criticism in the Hundred Flowers Movement, and caused a famine attempting to eradicate (*) sparrows in the Four Pests campaign. This leader promoted steel-making communes in the Great Leap Forward. This leader oversaw the Cultural Revolution and published many of his writings in The Little Red Book. For 10 points, name this former Chairman of the People’s Republic of China.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This leader remarked that “political power grows out of the barrel of a gun”. This leader also wrote On Guerrilla Warfare after being forced to retreat to the Jinggang Mountains due to the failed Autumn Harvest Uprising. This leader evaded (*) Chiang Kai-shek’s pursuits with the Red Army on the Long March. The Cultural Revolution and the Great Leap Forward were launched by, for ten points, what first leader of Communist China?
parts.answer: Mao Zedong [accept Mao Tse-Tung or Chairman Mao; prompt on Zedong or Tse-Tung]

topics.description: The Indigenous Polynesian people of Aotearoa New Zealand, associated with the Musket Wars and the signing of the Treaty of Waitangi with the British in 1840.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country formed an army corps with Australia that fought in the Gallipoli campaign and is honored on ANZAC Day. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this country, the location of silver ferns, which are featured on its airline’s planes and its coat of arms. This island country, whose capital is Wellington, is located southeast of Australia.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The silver fern is also a common motif in the art of these indigenous New Zealanders. These peoples signed the Treaty of Waitangi for peace with the British, and are often compared to Australian Aborigines.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The first European to sight New Zealand was this Dutch explorer. This explorer names an island just south of Australia, which was once known as Van Diemen’s Land.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A 2019 mass shooting at a mosque in this country's city of Christchurch made headlines worldwide. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country currently led by Jacinda Ardern from its capital of Wellington.

parts.label: B
parts.question: New Zealand is known as "Aotearoa" in the language of this indigenous Polynesian ethnic group, who fought each other in the Musket Wars and signed the Treaty of Waitangi in 1840 with British colonizers.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In 2015 and 2016, New Zealand undertook a pair of referendums on whether it should take this specific action, with "no" being the eventual result. Mississippi announced in 2020 that it would take this action in order to remove Confederate symbolism. A description is acceptable.
parts.answer: changing the flag [accept any obvious equivalents; accept answers like getting rid of the current flag]

topics.description: The legendary war in which Greek forces besieged Troy, traditionally sparked by Paris's abduction of Helen and ending with the Trojan Horse.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The protagonist of a 14th-century epic is led through this place by Virgil. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this place toured by Dante in the Inferno, where Dante witnesses sinners being punished.
parts.answer: Hell [or Christian hell; prompt on the underworld]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] In the second circle, Dante encounters those who committed this sin, such as Paolo and Francesca.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Along with Trajan, a participant in this war is the only pagan to reach heaven in Divine Comedy.  Other participants in this war suffer a double flame in the eighth circle, including one who gives a  speech about passing through the Pillars of Hercules.

topics.description: The 325 CE Christian ecumenical council that addressed the Arian controversy and produced the original form of the Nicene Creed.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This ruler organized an ecumenical council, whose namesake “Creed” affirms the belief in one god. A vision inspired this ruler to adopt the Chi Rho symbol before winning the Battle of Milvian Bridge. This ruler’s Edict of Milan officially (*) legalized Christianity within the Roman Empire. The first Chrisitan Roman Emperor was, for 10 points, what ruler, who names a city once called Byzantium and now called Istanbul?
parts.answer: Constantine the Great [or Constantine I; prompt on Constantine]

topics.description: An American automobile manufacturer founded by Henry Ford, known for the Model T, the River Rouge factory, and the Fordlandia project in Brazil.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 1930, native workers under this company cut telegraph lines and forced their managers to flee into the jungle during a revolt partly sparked by being forced to eat American food. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this company, whose founder invented the Model T.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Fordlandia was established in this country’s state of Pará. Getúlio Vargas served as the dictator of this non-European country during its Estado Novo period.
parts.answer: Brazil [or the Federative Republic of Brazil; or Republica Federativa do Brasil]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Fordlandia sought to harvest resources for this material that Ford Motors used in many of its operations, including to create the tires for their cars.

topics.description: British Conservative politician who served as Chancellor of the Exchequer and became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in October 2022.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about Boris Johnson’s resignation, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] In May 2022, Boris Johnson was fined for violating his own COVID-19 regulations during one of these events at 10 Downing Street in 2020. Finnish PM Sanna Marin attracted controversy for her conduct at one of these events.
parts.answer: parties [accept equivalents like social gatherings; accept Partygate]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In June 2022, 41 percent of this body’s Conservative members submitted no-confidence votes against Johnson. This body, divided into the House of Lords and the House of Commons, meets in the Palace of Westminster.
parts.answer: British Parliament [or Parliament of the United Kingdom]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Johnson resigned in July 2022 shortly after several ministers left his cabinet, including this former Chancellor of the Exchequer. This MP was announced as Liz Truss’s successor in October 2022.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country’s Conservative Party went into crisis in July 2022. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country, whose Prime Minister Boris Johnson resigned after suffering a record 62 cabinet resignations within the span of two days.
parts.answer: United Kingdom (or Great Britain; prompt on England)

parts.label: B
parts.question: This successor to Johnson as Prime Minister was on a plane to Indonesia during the onset of the crisis. This former Foreign Secretary was criticized in 2016 for her opposition to Brexit, though she later supported it.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In October 2022, this man became the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom. This former Chancellor of the Exchequer was among the first in Johnson’s cabinet to resign as a result of the Chris Pincher scandal.

topics.description: Piedmontese statesman and prime minister who used diplomacy and international alliances to advance the unification of Italy.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This cause defeated the black nobility that supported the independence of Pius IX. A supporter of this cause wrote an open letter to Charles Albert and was a member of the Carbonari. In the Plombières Agreement, Napoleon III agreed to support this cause at the behest of Count Cavour. At the battle of Calatafimi, supporters of this cause called Redshirts defeated the Kingdom of the Two (*) Sicilies. This cause was accomplished when Victor Emmanuel II ascended the throne of a new country with the support of Giuseppe Garibaldi. For 10 points, name this nationalist cause to create a new kingdom led from Rome.
parts.answer: Italian Unification [accept word forms such as the unification of Italy; or the Risorgimento]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: To garner international support for this cause, Count Cavour entered Piedmont-Sardinia into the Crimean War. The success of this cause resulted in the crowning of Victor-Emmanuel II as king. The Red Shirts advanced this cause under (*) Giuseppi Garibaldi by conquering the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. For 10 points, what 19th century cause sought to consolidate provinces like the Papal States and Venice into a single country?

topics.description: The 1982 war between Argentina and the United Kingdom over the Falkland Islands, known in Argentina as the Islas Malvinas.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A revolutionary born in this country had his photo taken after the La Coubre explosion by Alberto Korda.  This country’s descamisados were bombed in its Plaza de Mayo in 1955. A regime in this country waged the  (*) “Dirty War” against its political opponents under Jorge Videla, and later went to war with Britain over the  Falkland Islands. For 10 points, name this country led by Juan Peron from a pink palace in Buenos Aires.
parts.answer: Argentina [or Argentine Republic; or Republica Argentina]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country's capital contains the widest street in the world, the Ninth of July Avenue. Gauchos herd cattle on this country's pampas plains. This country shares the Iguazu Falls with Brazil and Paraguay, and it fought the UK in the (*) Falklands War. This country shares Patagonia with its western neighbor, Chile. For 10 points, what country is led from Buenos Aires?

topics.description: Pancho Villa, born José Doroteo Arango Arámbula, was a Mexican revolutionary leader who commanded the División del Norte during the Mexican Revolution.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This general played himself in a now-lost silent film produced by D.W. Griffith. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this Mexican revolutionary who caused the U.S. “Punitive Expedition” with his raid on  Columbus, New Mexico.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Pancho Villa [or Francisco Villa; or José Doroteo Arango Arámbula]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Pancho Villa joined Emiliano Zapata in a loose coalition devoted to reforming the distribution of  this resource in Mexico. Under the ejido (ay-HEE-doh) system, this resource is state-owned and peasants  have usage rights only.
parts.answer: ANSWER: land [or farmland; or agricultural land; or real property; or real estate; prompt on farms]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Ambassador Henry Lane Wilson backed this anti-democratic general's coup of Francisco Madero in  1913, though his presidency was not formally recognized by the U.S.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Victoriano Huerta [José Victoriano Huerta Márquez]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Mariano Azuela’s novel The Underdogs is likely the first novel about this conflict. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this conflict. Ambrose Bierce’s involvement and death in this conflict were fictionalized in The Old Gringo.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This Mexican author and key figure in the Latin American Boom wrote The Old Gringo. This author detailed the final hours of a veteran of the Mexican Revolution in The Death of Artemio Cruz.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This real-life bandit and Mexican revolutionary orders the death of General Arroyo in The Old Gringo. Azuela’s The Underdogs drew on his experience working as a doctor for this man, who is known by the nickname “Pancho.”
parts.answer: Pancho Villa [or Francisco Villa or José Doroteo Arango Arámbula]
